schemaHistory: 1.0 named the fields `newlyReached` and `rejected`. 1.1 renamed the second to `reachedButUnattested`, because `rejected` read as 'not reached'. 1.2 renamed the first to `reachedAndAttested`, because BOTH fields hold reached surfaces and `newlyReached` implied a contrast that does not exist. 1.3 adds `attestationEvidence`. Each rename is a SHAPE change and not an append, so the version moves each time — the match-behavior benchmark holds at 1.0 through case appends for the opposite reason. NOTE ON THIS FIELD: at 1.2 it wrongly said 1.0 had used `reachedAndAttested`, because a blanket rename edited the history describing the rename. Sol's fifth review caught it. The names above are the ones each version actually shipped.
question: Which word surfaces does comparing denylist entries and passage tokens as STEMS newly reach, beyond what the literal `entry` / `entry + s` tests already reached — and which of those are surfaces a real source could actually contain?
ruling: These, and this file is the vocabulary the answer is exhaustive OVER. Read `reachedAndAttested` + `reachedButUnattested` for what the comparison reaches; read `reachedAndAttested` alone for the part of it a source could actually contain. The v2.6.1 release report published this census three times as 'enumerated over all sixteen entries' and it was wrong every time: the first version named `pays`, which does not match, and omitted SEVEN surfaces (`hosters`, `networkers`, `clouding`, `payable`, `payed`, `serviceable`, `careers`) — an earlier draft of this ruling said six while naming seven, the same by-eye counting error one level up; the second version omitted `carefulness` and `medicalization`; the third omitted `internetization` and `networkization`. Sol found each set. All three failures were the same step — a candidate space generated mechanically and then filtered to real English BY HAND, where a hand that forgets a word leaves no trace. So the hand judgments are now the fixture. `tests/lab-match-behavior.test.mjs` regenerates the mechanical space from the stemmer's own suffix inventory and requires every candidate in it to carry an explicit verdict here, which is what makes an omission impossible rather than merely unlikely.
notExhaustiveOver: English. A surface is only in this file if the stemmer's suffix rules generate it from an entry or an entry's stem, so an irregular form reaching the same stem by another route would not appear — `paid` is the known example and it does not match anyway. Claims of exhaustiveness are about the generated space, never about the language.
twoFieldsTwoKindsOfClaim: THE REACH SET IS reachedAndAttested + reachedButUnattested, AND IT IS MECHANICAL. Every candidate in this file stems to its entry's stem, so the shipped comparison disqualifies every one of them today; that half is complete over the generated space and is not a matter of opinion. `attested` is the second, separate question — whether a real source could contain the surface — and it is a judgment that stays revisable. Moving a word between the two fields therefore changes NOTHING about what the instrument does or what this census claims to reach. It changes only which part of the widening is expected to be met in practice. Three review rounds were spent contesting word calls as though they bounded the reach; they never did, and the earlier field name `rejected` invited exactly that misreading.
wordStandard: For `reachedAndAttested`: listed in a standard English dictionary, or in settled technical use in the register the entry comes from. Arguable calls are recorded rather than applied silently, so a reviewer contests one word instead of the whole table, and they resolve toward the wider stated cost. Arguable and counted as attested: `hosters`, `payed`; `hostable` and `networkable`, added on Sol's second review; and `cloudable`, added on the third — Cisco's IBSG SMB cloud research uses "cloudable" spending for IT spend suitable for cloud delivery, which is settled enough for this register even though the scare quotes in the source show it began as a coinage. Everything in `reachedButUnattested` is still REACHED; it is only unlikely to appear in real text. Attested surfaces whose evidence was contested at any point carry it in `attestationEvidence` below, with a URL and a quoted phrase, so a reader checks the source rather than the maintainer. That field exists because the fifth review found two attestation rulings resting on nothing a reader could reproduce: one on a reviewer's citations that were never recorded, and one — `softwareization` — on a maintainer's ASSERTION ABOUT TWO DOCUMENTS HE HAD NOT OPENED. The second was wrong. Both ITU FG-NET2030 and ETSI White Paper 38 print `softwareization`, so it is attested and reached, and the earlier ruling against it is withdrawn.

bases: each base with no suffix at all
generator.suffixSource: The alternations inside stemToken's own `.replace(/(?:…)$/u, …)` chain in js/lab-analyzer.js, extracted from the source text by tests/lab-match-behavior.test.mjs and asserted equal to the list above. This list is therefore not a second copy that can drift: a suffix added to stemToken and not here fails the suite. It previously WAS a copy, and carried `er`, which stemToken does not strip — Sol's second review caught it. Dropping `er` changed no candidate, because nothing it generates survives the stem filter (`hoster` stems to `hoster`).
variants: the base with a final y replaced by i
generator.variantsSource: Generator convention, NOT a stemToken rule. stemToken maps a trailing `ies` to `y`; the y-to-i variant is how this generator produces the surfaces that rule accepts (`energies`, `utilities`). Declared rather than derived, because it is the one part of the space the stemmer's own text does not give.
generator.keep: candidates whose stem equals the entry's stem, excluding the entry itself and `entry + s` (both already reached by the literal tests)

internetization.note: Passaris' coinage; carried as a dictionary headword.

internetization.quote: Internetization as the necessary condition for internationalization in the newly emerging economy

networkization.source: The information revolution and the transformation of warfare (Elsevier, via ScienceDirect)
networkization.quote: The growing networkization of warfare is transforming

softwareization.quote: current trend of 'softwareization' in the network side

cloudable.source: Cisco IBSG, SMB public cloud adoption research
cloudable.note: Used of IT spending suitable for cloud delivery. Cisco's own scare quotes are retained here: the word was a coinage in that document.

hosters.source: settled trade usage in the hosting industry
hosters.note: No single citation recorded. The weakest evidence in this file now that the others carry sources, and the verdict most likely to be wrong next.

payed.source: standard dictionaries, as a nonstandard past form of `pay`
payed.note: Listed as a variant rather than as settled prose usage.

hostable.note: Reviewer-supplied at the third pass; the exact phrase was not re-verified by the maintainer.

networkable.note: Reviewer-supplied at the third pass, describing "networkable legacy printer models"; URL recorded in the review, not re-verified here.

maintainerErrorOfRecord: `softwareization` was ruled UNATTESTED at the fourth pass on the maintainer's claim that ITU and ETSI write `softwarization` instead. That claim was made from a general web search, without opening either document, and it was false: both print `softwareization`. It is recorded here rather than only in git because it is the fifth instance of the pattern this whole review arc has been correcting, and the first one the maintainer committed while CONTESTING the reviewer for the same class of error. A negative claim about a specific source requires reading that source.

realButNotReached.softwarization: Stems to `softwar`, so this denylist never sees it. It is a real term and a GAP in the widening rather than a cost of it — the mirror image of everything else in this file, which is reached whether or not it is attested. Recorded because a denylist that cannot see a live technical spelling is a finding in its own right, not an illustration.

entries.note: Multiword entries are matched as a contiguous run of two stems rather than as one token, so a single-surface census does not describe them. Their widening is a property of token SEQUENCES and is frozen as the branch truth table in tests/lab-match-behavior.test.mjs — `healthfulness carefulness` and `healths careers` are the sequences the stem run reaches and the literal and substring tests do not.
As `health care`. `childfulness carefulness` is the decisive sequence.
